2.r: Dative of the person with γίγνομαι: “a thought came to be ours”, the dative of the possessor [SMYTH:1476] [CONV:R2]. Read with the mental noun ἔννοια it could also be the person who experiences the thought (DatExpr), and Miller's “occurred to us” allows that [TR]; the possessive construction with γίγνομαι is the more regular one. Tree: the tree attaches ἡμῖν to ἔννοιά, not to ἐγένετο.

3.r: Aorist indicative stating a single past occurrence [SMYTH:1923]; γίγνομαι already means “come about”, so an ingressive reading adds little. γίγνομαι is middle-only and describes a change of state with no agent, the spontaneous-process middle [CONV:D3] [CONV:R1]. Indicative of a plain statement [MORPH].

4.r: ὅσαι agrees with δημοκρατίαι, the subject of κατελύθησαν, and takes its function [TREE].

5.r: Subject of κατελύθησαν in the indirect question “how many democracies were overthrown” [TREE].

6.r: Aorist passive indicative in an indirect question, which keeps the indicative [MORPH]. The aorist states the events as facts [SMYTH:1923]; the agent follows with ὑπό [SMYTH:1755], so the voice is passive.

8.r: τῶν makes the participle βουλομένων a noun, “those who wished” [SMYTH:1153]; it names a class only loosely, so ArtGener is a weak alternative [SMYTH:1124].

11.r: Genitive of the agent after ὑπό with the passive κατελύθησαν [SMYTH:1755]; the project tags this GenSep [CONV:D4] [PREP:ὑπό]. With τῶν it is a substantival participle, “those wishing” [SMYTH:2049]. Present participle outside indirect discourse: aspect only. βούλομαι is the card's own example of the mental-activity middle [CONV:D3].

12.r: Infinitive after the verb of will βουλομένων [SMYTH:1991], present for aspect, not in indirect discourse [SMYTH:1869]. πολιτεύεσθαι “live as a citizen, have one's form of government” is the middle of πολιτεύω [LSJ]; it can be read as acting in one's own interest (MidIndir) or as plain intransitive activity (Act). Tree: τῶν and βουλομένων hang on πολιτεύεσθαι; the phrase is τῶν … βουλομένων (object of ὑπό), and πολιτεύεσθαι is the object of βουλομένων.

16.r: ἐν δημοκρατίᾳ “under a democracy”: ἐν with the dative of the state one lives in [SMYTH:1687], tagged as place under the provisional rule for prepositions [CONV:D1] [PREP:ἐν].

18.r: Agrees with μοναρχίαι, a subject of ἀνῄρηνται [TREE].

21.r: Subject of ἀνῄρηνται, coordinated with ὀλιγαρχίαι [TREE].

23.r: Agrees with ὀλιγαρχίαι, a subject of ἀνῄρηνται [TREE].

25.r: Subject of ἀνῄρηνται, coordinated with μοναρχίαι [TREE].

26.r: Perfect indicative “have been abolished”, with ἤδη: the result still holds [MORPH]. The middle-passive form is passive here, with the agent ὑπὸ δήμων [SMYTH:1755].

29.r: Agent of the perfect passive ἀνῄρηνται, with ὑπό [SMYTH:1755]; tagged GenSep under the project rule [CONV:D4] [PREP:ὑπό].

32.r: ὅσοι … ἐπιχειρήσαντες names the whole group, which οἱ μὲν … οἱ δέ then divide: Holden calls this “partitive apposition to ὅσοι τυραννεῖν ἐπιχειρήσαντες” [COMM:en-holden-1887-books1-2-notes:13] [COMM:en-holden-shuckburgh-1902-book1:76] [SMYTH:981]. The whole stands as subject of the clause; because no verb takes it directly, a hanging nominative (NomInd) remains possible.

33.r: Infinitive completing ἐπιχειρέω “attempt to” [LSJ] [SMYTH:1991], not in indirect discourse, so aspect only. Active verb [MORPH].

34.r: Holden–Shuckburgh renders τυραννεῖν ἐπιχειρήσαντες “after setting up a despotism” [COMM:en-holden-shuckburgh-1902-book1:76]: a temporal circumstantial participle with ὅσοι [SMYTH:2054]. Without an article it is not attributive, though “those who attempted” is close. Its case follows ὅσοι (see there) [SMYTH:981].

35.r: οἱ μέν … οἱ δέ “some … others”: the article as demonstrative [SMYTH:1107], dividing ὅσοι, as Holden notes [COMM:en-holden-1887-books1-2-notes:13].

37.r: αὐτῶν “of them” with οἱ μέν: the genitive of the whole from which a part is taken [SMYTH:1306]. An oblique αὐτός standing alone is the personal pronoun [MORPH].

39.r: Holden: καὶ ταχὺ πάμπαν “very soon indeed: καί is intensive” [COMM:en-holden-1887-books1-2-notes:13] [COMM:en-holden-shuckburgh-1902-book1:76]. ταχύ is a neuter accusative used as an adverb [SMYTH:1606].

41.r: Aorist passive indicative “were overthrown”, still inside the indirect question, which keeps the indicative [MORPH] [SMYTH:1923].

43.r: The second half of οἱ μέν … οἱ δέ, the article as demonstrative [SMYTH:1107].

47.r: Agrees with χρόνον and shares its function, extent of time [SMYTH:1582].

48.r: ὁποσονοῦν χρόνον “for however short a time”: accusative of extent of time [SMYTH:1582] [TR].

49.r: διαγένωνται ἄρχοντες “continue ruling”: διαγίγνομαι takes a supplementary participle [SMYTH:2097] [SMYTH:2088]. The participle agrees with the subject οἱ δέ; the tree makes it a predicate (PNOM), which is why NomPred stays as the alternative [TREE].

50.r: κἂν (καὶ ἐάν) with the subjunctive: a general condition [SMYTH:2337], so SubjSubor [CONV:D6]; the aorist gives aspect only. διαγίγνομαι is a middle-only compound of γίγνομαι, so the project classes it as a spontaneous-process middle [CONV:D3]; its sense “continue” leaves Act possible.

52.r: Present passive indicative “they are admired” [MORPH]. It states what generally happens to such rulers, so the customary present is a real alternative [SMYTH:1876]; the plain tag is kept under the project default [CONV:D2].

54.r: σοφοί agrees with ἄνδρες, the predicate of γεγενημένοι “having proved wise men”, and takes its function [SMYTH:1040].

57.r: Like σοφοί: part of the predicate of γεγενημένοι [SMYTH:1040].

58.r: Predicate noun with γεγενημένοι, a verb of becoming [SMYTH:1040] [TREE].

59.r: ὡς γεγενημένοι “as having proved”: a circumstantial participle of cause, given as others see it [SMYTH:2054]. It agrees with the subject of θαυμάζονται. Perfect participle outside indirect discourse: aspect of completed state [SMYTH:1872]. Voice as for γίγνομαι [CONV:D3] [CONV:R1].

62.r: πολλούς is what was observed: subject of the participles ἔχοντας and δυναμένους in indirect discourse after καταμεμαθηκέναι [SMYTH:2106] [TREE]. Holden–Shuckburgh notes πολλούς … τοὺς μέν … τοὺς δέ as the same whole-and-part pattern as before [COMM:en-holden-shuckburgh-1902-book1:77]. As the object of the verb of learning, AccObj is close.

64.r: Imperfect indicative “we thought”, a state continuing in the past [SMYTH:1890]. Active verb, plain statement [MORPH].

65.r: δοκέω “think” with the infinitive reports a thought: indirect discourse [SMYTH:1867]. The infinitive keeps the tense of “we have observed”, so Perf, not PerfNoni [CONV:D7].

68.r: Agrees with οἴκοις: “in private households also”, as Holden–Shuckburgh renders it [COMM:en-holden-shuckburgh-1902-book1:77] [PREP:ἐν] [CONV:D1].

69.r: ἐν with the dative of place [SMYTH:1687]; οἶκος is “household” rather than “house”, as Holden–Shuckburgh points out [COMM:en-holden-shuckburgh-1902-book1:77] [PREP:ἐν] [CONV:D1].

70.r: τοὺς μὲν ἔχοντας … τοὺς δέ: the article both makes the participle a noun, “those who have” [SMYTH:1153], and does the work of ὁ μέν … ὁ δέ [SMYTH:1107], dividing πολλούς [COMM:en-holden-shuckburgh-1902-book1:77]. The two functions coincide here, so the certainty is split.

72.r: With τούς, a substantival participle “those who have” [SMYTH:2049], in apposition to πολλούς and sharing its case function [SMYTH:981]. It describes, it does not report, so its present gives aspect only.

74.r: Agrees with οἰκέτας, the object of ἔχοντας [TREE].

75.r: Direct object of ἔχοντας “having more servants” [TREE].

77.r: τοὺς δέ (with ἔχοντας understood): the second half of the division, as with τοὺς μέν [SMYTH:1107] [SMYTH:1153].

81.r: Object of the understood ἔχοντας: “others (having) very few” [TREE].

87.r: τοῖς ὀλίγοις τούτοις “these few”: the article makes ὀλίγοις a noun [SMYTH:1153], and at the same time points back to the few just mentioned [SMYTH:1120]. Holden–Shuckburgh: “not even these few, much less a larger number” [COMM:en-holden-shuckburgh-1902-book1:77].

88.r: Agrees with τούτοις, the dative object of χρῆσθαι [SMYTH:1509].

89.r: χρῆσθαι “use, deal with” takes the dative [SMYTH:1509] [LSJ].

91.r: πάνυ τι “at all”: Holden glosses οὐδὲ … πάνυ τι as “not even these few at all” [COMM:en-holden-1887-books1-2-notes:14]. τι is an adverbial accusative [SMYTH:1606].

92.r: After καταμεμαθηκέναι “we had observed that …” the participle reports what was learnt: indirect discourse [SMYTH:2106], so its tense keeps its time value [SMYTH:1874] [CONV:D7]. It agrees with πολλούς. δύναμαι is middle-only and fits none of the middle types well [CONV:R3].

93.r: Infinitive completing δυναμένους “able to”, not in indirect discourse, so aspect only. χράομαι is a middle-only verb of using “for oneself”, which Smyth groups with the indirect middles [SMYTH:1730] [CONV:D3].

94.r: χρῆσθαι πειθομένοις: Bigg renders it “to profit by their obedience … to maintain discipline among them” [COMM:en-bigg-1888-book1:79]. πειθομένοις agrees with the dative object τούτοις [SMYTH:1509] and says in what state they are used, between a supplementary and a circumstantial participle. πείθομαι “obey” could be read as a mental middle, as a passive “be persuaded”, or as reflexive “persuade oneself”; the evidence does not decide.

95.r: τοὺς δεσπότας “the masters”, the particular masters of these households [SMYTH:1120] [COMM:en-bigg-1888-book1:79].

96.r: Bigg: “τοὺς δεσπότας is added in apposition to τοὺς δέ for the sake of a little more distinctness, ‘I mean the masters’” [COMM:en-bigg-1888-book1:79]. So it shares the function of πολλούς and τοὺς δέ, the subject of the reported participles [SMYTH:981]. πείθομαι takes the dative, so it cannot be the object of πειθομένοις. Tree: attached as OBJ of πειθομένοις; it is in apposition to τοὺς δέ / πολλούς (Bigg).

102.r: Dative with πρός, “near; in addition to” [PREP:πρός]. No Didakta tag names this prepositional use; DatLoc is the closest [CONV:D1].

103.r: Imperfect of continued past action [SMYTH:1890]. Active voice [MORPH]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

105.r: ἄρχοντες is used as a noun, “rulers”, the predicate with εἰσι [SMYTH:2050]. Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH].

107.r: Present indicative of a present or general fact [MORPH]. Active voice [MORPH]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

109.r: Generic article: βουκόλοι as a whole class [SMYTH:1122].

111.r: τῶν βοῶν “of (their) cattle”: the class as a whole [SMYTH:1122]; Miller's “their cattle” takes the article as possessive [TR].

112.r: ἄρχοντες … τῶν βοῶν: ἄρχω governs the genitive [LSJ] [SMYTH:1370]. Since ἄρχοντες is here a noun, “rulers of the cattle”, the genitive can also be taken as objective.

114.r: Generic article: ἱπποφορβοὶ as a whole class [SMYTH:1122].

116.r: τῶν ἵππων “of (their) horses”: the class as a whole [SMYTH:1122]; Miller's “their horses” takes the article as possessive [TR].

117.r: With ἄρχοντες understood from the first member: ἄρχω governs the genitive [LSJ] [SMYTH:1370]; with the participle felt as a noun the genitive can also be taken as objective.

122.r: The article makes πάντες a substantive [SMYTH:1153].

123.n: TREE: the postag should be v-pppemn- (tree: v-pfpmmn-).
123.r: οἱ καλούμενοι νομεῖς “those who are called herdsmen”: attributive participle with the article, passive of καλέω with the predicate noun νομεῖς [SMYTH:2050]. Agrees with πάντες and takes its case function [TREE]. Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859].

125.r: ὧν … ζῴων: ἐπιστατέω “be set over” governs the genitive [LSJ] [SMYTH:1370]; the antecedent ζῴων is drawn into the relative clause.

127.r: Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH]. Subjunctive in a subordinate clause [CONV:D6].

128.r: ζῴων is the antecedent taken into the relative clause, in the case of ὧν [SMYTH:2536]; it is resumed by τούτων, which depends on ἄρχοντες.

131.r: ἄρχοντες is used as a noun, “rulers”, the predicate with νομίζοιντο [SMYTH:2050]. Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH].

132.n: TREE: τούτων depends on ἄρχοντες, not on ζῴων as in the tree.
132.r: ἄρχοντες τούτων “rulers of these”: τούτων resumes ὧν … ζῴων. ἄρχω governs the genitive [LSJ] [SMYTH:1370]; with the participle felt as a noun the genitive can also be taken as objective.

133.r: Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Passive: the subject is acted on [SMYTH:1735]. Potential optative with ἄν [SMYTH:1824].

137.n: TREE: the postag should be a-p---fa- (tree: a-s---fg-).
137.r: Agrees with ἀγέλας and takes its case function [TREE].

139.r: Agrees with ἀγέλας and takes its case function [TREE].

140.r: Particular article: ἀγέλας is a definite, identifiable referent [SMYTH:1119].

141.r: ὁρᾶν … τὰς ἀγέλας … ἐθελούσας “to see that the herds are more willing”: object of ὁρᾶν and subject of the participle [SMYTH:2110]; with a supplementary participle the noun is taken as the object [CONV:R4].

142.r: Imperfect of continued past action [SMYTH:1890]. Active voice [MORPH]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

143.r: ἐδοκοῦμεν ὁρᾶν “we thought we saw”: infinitive of indirect discourse after δοκέω [SMYTH:1983], so the present keeps its tense value [CONV:D7]. Active voice [MORPH].

145.r: ἐθελούσας gives what was seen: supplementary participle in indirect discourse after ὁρᾶν [SMYTH:2110]. It agrees with ἀγέλας. In indirect discourse the tense is that of the direct form [CONV:D7]. Active voice [MORPH].

146.r: Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. πείθομαι “obey, trust”: a middle of mental process; it can also be read as passive “be persuaded” [CONV:D3]. Dynamic infinitive completing ἐθελούσας [SMYTH:1989].

147.r: Particular article: νομεῦσιν is a definite, identifiable referent [SMYTH:1119].

150.r: Generic article: ἀνθρώπους as a whole class [SMYTH:1122].

151.r: τοὺς ἀνθρώπους stands in the second member of the comparison, parallel to τὰς ἀγέλας, with ἐθέλοντας πείθεσθαι understood [CONV:R4].

152.r: The article makes ἄρχουσι a substantive [SMYTH:1153].

153.r: Dative governed by the verb understood [SMYTH:1460]. Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH]. Attributive or substantival participle [SMYTH:2049].

157.r: A general statement about herds: the present of a standing fact, which can also be felt as customary [SMYTH:1877]. πορεύομαι “march, go” is a middle of motion [CONV:D3]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

160.r: αἱ ἀγέλαι “herds” as a class in a general statement [SMYTH:1122]; it also points back to ταύτας τὰς ἀγέλας just mentioned.

164.r: Direct object of εὐθύνωσιν [TREE]. Oblique αὐτός standing alone: the personal pronoun “him, her, it, them” [SMYTH:1212].

165.r: Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH]. Subjunctive in a subordinate clause [CONV:D6].

166.r: Generic article: νομεῖς as a whole class [SMYTH:1122].

169.r: A general statement about herds: the present of a standing fact, which can also be felt as customary [SMYTH:1877]. νέμομαι “graze, feed on, have as one's portion”: the subject takes something for itself, an indirect reflexive middle [SMYTH:1719]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

173.r: Accusative with ἐπί, “to, against”: motion towards [PREP:ἐπί]; the tag gives the function of the phrase [CONV:D1].

175.r: Direct object of ἐπάγωσιν [TREE]. Oblique αὐτός standing alone: the personal pronoun “him, her, it, them” [SMYTH:1212].

176.r: Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH]. Subjunctive in a subordinate clause [CONV:D6].

178.r: A general statement about herds: the present of a standing fact, which can also be felt as customary [SMYTH:1877]. ἀπέχομαι “hold oneself off, abstain”: the subject acts on itself [SMYTH:1717]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

180.r: ὧν = (τούτων) ὧν: the genitive of separation with ἀπέχονται and ἀπείργωσι, “keep away from those from which they shut them out” [SMYTH:1392]. Holden–Shuckburgh: “ἀπέχονται, sc. χωρίων” [COMM:en-holden-shuckburgh-1902-book1:77]. A genitive governed by a verb of separating can also be classed as GenVerb [CONV:R8].

182.r: Direct object of ἀπείργωσι [TREE]. Oblique αὐτός standing alone: the personal pronoun “him, her, it, them” [SMYTH:1212].

183.r: Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH]. Subjunctive in a subordinate clause [CONV:D6].

186.r: Particular article: καρποῖς is a definite, identifiable referent [SMYTH:1119].

189.r: Particular article: καρποῖς is a definite, identifiable referent [SMYTH:1119].

190.r: Agrees with καρποῖς and takes its case function [TREE]. Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. γίγνομαι is middle-only and denotes a change of state without an agent: the spontaneous-process middle [CONV:D3] [CONV:R1]. Attributive or substantival participle [SMYTH:2049].

192.r: Genitive with ἐκ, “out of, from”: source or separation [PREP:ἐκ]; the tag gives the function of the phrase [CONV:D1]. Oblique αὐτός standing alone: the personal pronoun “him, her, it, them” [SMYTH:1212].

193.r: A general statement: the present of a standing fact, which can also be felt as customary [SMYTH:1877]. Active voice [MORPH]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

194.r: Particular article: νομέας is a definite, identifiable referent [SMYTH:1119].

196.r: Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. χράομαι “use” is middle-only: the subject avails itself of something, an indirect reflexive middle [CONV:D3]. Dynamic infinitive completing ἐῶσι [SMYTH:1989].

201.r: Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. βούλομαι “wish” is middle-only, a middle of mental activity [CONV:D3]. Subjunctive in a subordinate clause [CONV:D6].

205.r: Agrees with ἀγέλην and takes its case function [TREE].

207.r: οὐδεμίαν ἀγέλην ᾐσθήμεθα συστᾶσαν “we have never perceived any herd to have conspired”: object of ᾐσθήμεθα and subject of the participle [SMYTH:2110] [CONV:R4].

208.n: TREE: the postag should be v1prim--- (tree: v1plim---).
208.r: ᾐσθήμεθα can be perfect or pluperfect in form; with πώποτε and the present εἰσιν that follows it is the perfect, as Holden translates: “I never yet at any time have known of a herd combining” [COMM:en-holden-1887-books1-2-notes:15]. αἰσθάνομαι “perceive” is middle-only, a middle of perception [CONV:D3]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

209.r: συστᾶσαν gives what was perceived: supplementary participle in indirect discourse after αἰσθάνομαι [SMYTH:2110]; it agrees with ἀγέλην. In indirect discourse the tense is that of the direct form [CONV:D7]. Active voice [MORPH].

211.r: τὸν νομέα “its herdsman”: the article for the possessive, the possessor being plain [SMYTH:1121]; it can also be the keeper already spoken of.

212.r: ἐπὶ τὸν νομέα “against its herdsman”: ἐπί with the accusative of hostile direction [PREP:ἐπί] [CONV:D1].

217.r: ὡς μὴ πείθεσθαι “so as not to obey”: infinitive of result with ὡς [SMYTH:2260]. Bigg: “ὡς has here a limiting sense: we have never seen them conspire either so as to disobey …” [COMM:en-bigg-1888-book1:79]. Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. πείθομαι “obey, trust”: a middle of mental process; it can also be read as passive “be persuaded” [CONV:D3].

222.r: ὡς μὴ ἐπιτρέπειν “so as not to allow”: infinitive of result with ὡς, parallel to πείθεσθαι [SMYTH:2260] [COMM:en-bigg-1888-book1:79]. Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH].

223.r: Particular article: καρπῷ is a definite, identifiable referent [SMYTH:1119].

225.r: Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. χράομαι “use” is middle-only: the subject avails itself of something, an indirect reflexive middle [CONV:D3]. Dynamic infinitive completing ἐπιτρέπειν [SMYTH:1989].

230.r: Present indicative of a present or general fact [MORPH]. Active voice [MORPH]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

231.r: Generic article: ἀγέλαι as a whole class [SMYTH:1122].

233.r: Agrees with ἀλλοφύλοις and takes its case function [TREE].

234.r: The article makes ἀλλοφύλοις a substantive [SMYTH:1153].

235.r: χαλεπώτεραι … τοῖς ἀλλοφύλοις “harder towards strangers”: the dative of the person to whose disadvantage the quality tells, with an adjective of hostile disposition [SMYTH:1499] [SMYTH:1481].

237.r: The article makes ἄρχουσί a substantive [SMYTH:1153].

238.r: Agrees with ἀλλοφύλοις and takes its case function [TREE]. Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH]. Attributive or substantival participle [SMYTH:2049].

241.r: τοῖς ἄρχουσί τε καὶ ὠφελουμένοις share one article: “those who rule them and get profit from them”, a substantival participle in the second member of the comparison with τοῖς ἀλλοφύλοις [SMYTH:2050]. Passive: Holden–Shuckburgh, “those who receive benefits from them. ὑπό would imply direct agency” [COMM:en-holden-shuckburgh-1902-book1:77]. Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859].

243.r: Genitive with ἀπό, “from”: source or separation [PREP:ἀπό]; the tag gives the function of the phrase [CONV:D1]. Oblique αὐτός standing alone: the personal pronoun “him, her, it, them” [SMYTH:1212].

249.r: ἐπʼ οὐδένας “against none”: ἐπί with the accusative of hostile direction [PREP:ἐπί] [CONV:D1].

251.r: A general statement about men: the present of a standing fact, which can also be felt as customary [SMYTH:1877]. συνίσταμαι “band together”: a middle of collective motion; combining is also a mutual action [CONV:D3]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

254.r: ἐπὶ τούτους “against those”: ἐπί with the accusative of hostile direction [PREP:ἐπί] [CONV:D1].

255.r: οὓς ἂν αἴσθωνται … ἐπιχειροῦντας “whom they perceive attempting”: object of αἴσθωνται and subject of the participle [SMYTH:2110] [CONV:R4].

257.r: Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. αἰσθάνομαι “perceive” is middle-only, a middle of perception [CONV:D3]. Subjunctive in a subordinate clause [CONV:D6].

258.r: Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH]. Dynamic infinitive completing ἐπιχειροῦντας [SMYTH:1989].

260.r: ἐπιχειροῦντας gives what is perceived: supplementary participle in indirect discourse after αἰσθάνομαι [SMYTH:2110]; it agrees with οὕς. In indirect discourse the tense is that of the direct form [CONV:D7]. Active voice [MORPH].

267.r: Imperfect of continued past action [SMYTH:1890]. ἐνθυμέομαι is middle-only, a middle of mental activity [CONV:D3]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

270.r: Imperfect of continued past action [SMYTH:1890]. Active voice [MORPH]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

272.r: Genitive with περί, “about, concerning” [PREP:περί]. No Didakta tag names this prepositional use; GenRef is the closest [CONV:D1]. Oblique αὐτός standing alone: the personal pronoun “him, her, it, them” [SMYTH:1212].

275.r: ἀνθρώπῳ … ῥᾷον εἴη “it is easier for man”: the dative of the person for whom the statement holds, with the predicate ῥᾷον [SMYTH:1481]; it can also be taken as the dative of relation [SMYTH:1496].

276.r: ἀνθρώπῳ πεφυκότι “for man, being what he is by nature”: Miller, “for man, as he is constituted” [TR]. The participle limits the statement to man as man, so it is circumstantial rather than a plain attribute. Agrees with ἀνθρώπῳ and takes its case function [TREE]. Perfect stem outside the indicative: a completed state [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH].

277.r: Agrees with ζῴων and takes its case function [TREE].

278.r: Particular article: ζῴων is a definite, identifiable referent [SMYTH:1119].

279.r: Agrees with ζῴων and takes its case function [TREE].

280.n: TREE: the postag should be a-s---nnc (tree: a-s---nac).
280.r: ῥᾷον is neuter nominative, the predicate of εἴη, whose subject is the infinitive ἄρχειν [SMYTH:1985] [SMYTH:910].

281.r: Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH]. Optative in a subordinate clause [CONV:D6].

285.r: ἄρχειν is the subject of ῥᾷον εἴη, “to rule … is easier” [SMYTH:1985]. Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH].

290.r: Aorist indicative stating a single past event [SMYTH:1923]. Active voice [MORPH]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

293.r: ὅτι Κῦρος ἐγένετο Πέρσης: Bigg, “that there was one Cyrus a Persian” [COMM:en-bigg-1888-book1:79]. Aorist of a past fact. γίγνομαι is middle-only and denotes a change of state without an agent: the spontaneous-process middle [CONV:D3] [CONV:R1]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

294.r: Πέρσης stands with ἐγένετο, “there was a Cyrus, a Persian”; Holden takes the clause as equal to Κῦρος Πέρσης γενόμενος ἐκτήσατο [COMM:en-holden-1887-books1-2-notes:15]. As the noun completing ἐγένετο it is a predicate; read as “there arose Cyrus, a Persian” it is in apposition to the subject.

297.r: Agrees with ἀνθρώπους and takes its case function [TREE].

300.r: Aorist indicative stating a single past event [SMYTH:1923]. κτάομαι “acquire (for oneself)” is middle-only, an indirect reflexive middle [CONV:D3]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

301.r: ἀνθρώπους ἐκτήσατο πειθομένους αὑτῷ “he got men to be his obedient subjects”: the participle is predicative to the object, giving the state in which he acquired them; it can also be read as a plain attribute, “men who obeyed him”. Miller: “reduced to obedience a vast number of men” [TR]. Agrees with ἀνθρώπους and takes its case function [TREE]. Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. πείθομαι “obey, trust”: a middle of mental process; it can also be read as passive “be persuaded” [CONV:D3].

304.r: Agrees with πόλεις and takes its case function [TREE].

308.r: Agrees with ἔθνη and takes its case function [TREE].

313.r: Genitive with ἐκ, “out of, from”: source or separation [PREP:ἐκ]; the tag gives the function of the phrase [CONV:D1].

315.r: Imperfect of continued past action [SMYTH:1890]. Passive: the subject is acted on [SMYTH:1735]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

316.r: Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH]. Dynamic infinitive completing ἠναγκαζόμεθα [SMYTH:1989].

320.n: TREE: τῶν depends on ἔργων, not on ἀδυνάτων as in the tree.
320.r: τῶν ἀδυνάτων … ἔργων “(one) of the impossible tasks”: the article marks the whole class of such tasks [SMYTH:1122]. The tree attaches it to the adjective, which would make it a substantivizer.

321.r: Agrees with ἔργων and takes its case function [TREE].

324.n: TREE: τῶν depends on ἔργων, not on χαλεπῶν as in the tree.
324.r: τῶν χαλεπῶν ἔργων “(one) of the difficult tasks”: the article marks the whole class [SMYTH:1122]. The tree attaches it to the adjective, which would make it a substantivizer.

325.r: Agrees with ἔργων and takes its case function [TREE].

326.r: Predicate genitive with ᾖ: “whether to rule men is not among the impossible or the difficult tasks”, the partitive genitive as predicate [SMYTH:1319].

327.r: Subjunctive after μή: Bigg, “μετανοεῖν μὴ … ᾖ: to change my mind (and reflect) whether it is perhaps neither an impossibility nor a very difficult thing. The subjunctive depends upon the μή” [COMM:en-bigg-1888-book1:79]. A subordinate subjunctive [CONV:D6]. Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH].

328.r: τό makes the infinitive phrase ἀνθρώπων ἄρχειν a noun; Holden: “the articular infinitive forming the subject of ᾖ” [COMM:en-holden-1887-books1-2-notes:16].

330.r: Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH]. Articular infinitive [SMYTH:2025].

336.r: Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH]. Subjunctive in a subordinate clause [CONV:D6].

340.r: οἶδα is a perfect with present meaning [SMYTH:1946]; the plain tag is kept, with the intensive perfect as the alternative [CONV:R6]. Active voice [MORPH]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

341.n: TREE: ἐθελήσαντας depends on ἴσμεν, not on δὲ as in the tree.
341.r: ἴσμεν ἐθελήσαντας “we know that they were willing”: supplementary participle in indirect discourse after οἶδα [SMYTH:2106]; Holden notes the construction ἴσμεν ἐθελήσαντας [COMM:en-holden-1887-books1-2-notes:16]. It agrees with the persons divided by τοὺς μέν … τοὺς δέ, who are the object of ἴσμεν [CONV:R4]. In indirect discourse the tense is that of the direct form [CONV:D7]. Active voice [MORPH].

342.n: TREE: πείθεσθαι depends on ἐθελήσαντας, not on ἴσμεν as in the tree.
342.r: πείθεσθαι completes ἐθελήσαντας, “willing to obey” [SMYTH:1991]. Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. πείθομαι “obey, trust”: a middle of mental process; it can also be read as passive “be persuaded” [CONV:D3].

343.r: τοὺς μέν … τοὺς δέ “some … others”: the article as a pronoun [SMYTH:1107]; Holden translates “though some of them were distant many days' journey” [COMM:en-holden-1887-books1-2-notes:16].

345.r: ἀπέχοντας is concessive, as Holden renders it: “though some of them were distant many days' journey” [COMM:en-holden-1887-books1-2-notes:16]. It agrees with τοὺς μέν, the persons known [CONV:R4]. Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH].

346.r: Agrees with ἡμερῶν and takes its case function [TREE].

347.r: παμπόλλων ἡμερῶν ὁδόν “a journey of very many days”: genitive of measure [SMYTH:1325].

348.r: ἀπέχοντας … ὁδόν “distant a journey”: accusative of extent of space [SMYTH:1581].

350.r: τοὺς δέ: the article as a pronoun, continuing τοὺς μέν [SMYTH:1107].

353.r: (ὁδὸν) μηνῶν “a journey of months”: genitive of measure, with ὁδόν understood [SMYTH:1325].

355.r: τοὺς δέ: the article as a pronoun, continuing τοὺς μέν [SMYTH:1107].

358.r: οὐδʼ ἑωρακότας “though they had never even seen him”: concessive circumstantial participle, parallel to ἀπέχοντας [SMYTH:2066]. It agrees with τοὺς δέ, the persons known [CONV:R4]. Perfect stem outside the indicative: a completed state [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH].

360.r: Direct object of ἑωρακότας [TREE]. Oblique αὐτός standing alone: the personal pronoun “him, her, it, them” [SMYTH:1212].

362.r: τοὺς δέ: the article as a pronoun, continuing τοὺς μέν [SMYTH:1107].

366.r: εὖ εἰδότας is concessive; Holden: “though they knew full well that they could not see him either” [COMM:en-holden-1887-books1-2-notes:16]. It agrees with τοὺς δέ, the persons known [CONV:R4]. Perfect stem outside the indicative: a completed state [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH].

370.r: οὐδʼ ἂν ἴδοιεν “they could not even see him”: potential optative; Holden speaks of “the suppressed condition or protasis with οὐδʼ ἂν ἴδοιεν” [COMM:en-holden-1887-books1-2-notes:16]. Aorist stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as a single whole [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH].

374.r: ἤθελον continues the thought in a finite verb; Holden: “for ἤθελον the participle might have been used” [COMM:en-holden-1887-books1-2-notes:16]. Imperfect of a continued state of willingness [SMYTH:1890]. Active voice [MORPH]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

375.r: ὑπακούειν “obey” takes the dative [LSJ]. Oblique αὐτός standing alone: the personal pronoun “him, her, it, them” [SMYTH:1212].

376.r: Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH]. Dynamic infinitive completing ἤθελον [SMYTH:1989].

383.r: τοσοῦτον διήνεγκε: Holden, “he was so greatly superior to all other kings” [COMM:en-holden-1887-books1-2-notes:16]. Adverbial accusative of degree [SMYTH:1609].

384.r: διήνεγκε sums up his whole career in one statement, so the aorist can be felt as complexive [SMYTH:1927]; the plain aorist of a past fact is kept first [CONV:D2]. Active voice [MORPH]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

385.r: Particular article: βασιλέων is a definite, identifiable referent [SMYTH:1119].

386.r: Agrees with βασιλέων and takes its case function [TREE].

387.r: διήνεγκε τῶν ἄλλων βασιλέων “he surpassed the other kings”: the genitive with a verb of superiority, which implies a comparison [SMYTH:1402]; Holden cites the construction with “so greatly superior to” [COMM:en-holden-1887-books1-2-notes:16]. It is also simply the genitive governed by διαφέρω [LSJ], and “differ from” is at bottom separation.

390.n: TREE: τῶν depends on παρειληφότων, not on βασιλέων as in the tree.
390.r: The article makes παρειληφότων a substantive [SMYTH:1153].

391.r: Agrees with ἀρχὰς and takes its case function [TREE].

393.r: τῶν … παρειληφότων “those who have inherited thrones”: substantival participle in apposition to βασιλέων, taking its case function [SMYTH:2050]. Perfect stem outside the indicative: a completed state [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH].

395.n: TREE: τῶν depends on κτησαμένων, not on βασιλέων as in the tree.
395.r: The article makes κτησαμένων a substantive [SMYTH:1153].

397.r: διʼ ἑαυτῶν “by their own efforts”: διά with the genitive of the intermediary or means [PREP:διά]. No Didakta tag names this use; the agent-like source (GenSep, as for ὑπό) is the closest [CONV:D1] [CONV:D4].

398.r: τῶν … κτησαμένων “those who have won (their thrones)”: substantival participle in apposition to βασιλέων [SMYTH:2050]. Aorist stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as a single whole [SMYTH:1859]. κτάομαι “acquire (for oneself)” is middle-only, an indirect reflexive middle [CONV:D3].

401.r: ὁ Σκύθης “the Scythian (king)”: the article with an ethnic name standing for the one ruler, as Miller's “the Scythian king” [TR]. An ethnic name can also be classed with proper names.

405.r: Agrees with Σκυθῶν and takes its case function [TREE].

406.r: καίπερ παμπόλλων ὄντων Σκυθῶν “although the Scythians are very numerous”: a concessive genitive absolute [SMYTH:2070]. The tree hangs ὄντων on Σκυθῶν as an attribute. Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH].

407.n: TREE: Σκυθῶν depends on ὄντων, not on ἄλλου as in the tree.

408.r: Agrees with ἔθνους and takes its case function [TREE].

410.r: Agrees with ἔθνους and takes its case function [TREE].

411.r: οὐ δύναιτʼ ἄν: potential optative in the ὥστε clause; Holden, “could not possibly, the protasis being implied” [COMM:en-holden-1887-books1-2-notes:17]. It stays potential in a subordinate clause [CONV:D6]. Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. δύναμαι “be able” is middle-only and fits none of the middle types well; the case is still open [CONV:D3] [CONV:R3].

413.r: ἐπάρξαι “extend one's rule over” governs the genitive [SMYTH:1370].

414.r: Aorist stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as a single whole [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH]. Dynamic infinitive completing δύναιτʼ [SMYTH:1989].

416.r: Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH]. Potential optative with ἄν [SMYTH:1824].

420.r: Particular article: ἔθνους is a definite, identifiable referent [SMYTH:1119].

423.r: ἄρχων διαγένοιτο “continue ruling”: supplementary participle with διαγίγνομαι [SMYTH:2097], agreeing with the subject; Holden refers back to the same phrase in § 1 [COMM:en-holden-1887-books1-2-notes:17]. Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH].

424.r: Aorist stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as a single whole [SMYTH:1859]. διαγίγνομαι is a compound of γίγνομαι, middle-only: the spontaneous-process middle [CONV:D3] [CONV:R1]. Optative in a subordinate clause [CONV:D6].

427.r: ὁ Θρᾷξ “the Thracian (king)”: the article with an ethnic name standing for the one ruler [TR]. An ethnic name can also be classed with proper names.

429.r: Holden supplies the construction: “in full, ὁ Θρᾷξ ἀγαπῴη ἄν, εἰ τῶν Θρᾳκῶν … ἄρχων διαγένοιτο” [COMM:en-holden-1887-books1-2-notes:17]. The genitive is governed by ἄρχων understood [SMYTH:1370].

431.r: ὁ Ἰλλυριός “the Illyrian (king)”: the article with an ethnic name standing for the one ruler [TR]. An ethnic name can also be classed with proper names.

433.r: Parallel to Θρᾳκῶν: the genitive is governed by ἄρχων understood [COMM:en-holden-1887-books1-2-notes:17] [SMYTH:1370].

436.r: τἆλλα ἔθνη “the other nations”, the rest as a definite body [SMYTH:1188].

437.r: Agrees with ἔθνη and takes its case function [TREE].

440.r: τἆλλα … ἔθνη ὡσαύτως ἀκούομεν “and the other nations likewise, we hear”: an infinitive is understood from what precedes, of which ἔθνη is the subject [SMYTH:1972]; Miller: “and so also all other nations, we are told” [TR]. Taken closely with ἀκούομεν it is its object.

441.r: ἀκούομεν “we hear, we are told”: the present of a verb of hearing whose action began in the past and whose effect continues [SMYTH:1885]. Active voice [MORPH]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

445.r: τὰ ἐν τῇ Εὐρώπῃ (sc. ἔθνη): the article makes the prepositional phrase a noun [SMYTH:1153]; Holden–Shuckburgh: “at least those in Europe” [COMM:en-holden-shuckburgh-1902-book1:79].

448.r: Article with the proper name Εὐρώπῃ [SMYTH:1136].

449.r: Dative with ἐν, “in, at”: place where [PREP:ἐν]; the tag gives the function of the phrase [CONV:D1].

454.r: αὐτόνομα εἶναι λέγεται “are said to be independent”: infinitive of indirect discourse with the personal passive λέγεται [SMYTH:1982]. In indirect discourse the tense is that of the direct form [CONV:D7]. Active voice [MORPH].

455.r: Present indicative of a present or general fact [MORPH]. Passive: the subject is acted on [SMYTH:1735]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

457.r: λελύσθαι “to be free of one another”, parallel to εἶναι: infinitive of indirect discourse with λέγεται [SMYTH:1982]. In indirect discourse the tense is that of the direct form [CONV:D7].

459.r: Genitive with ἀπό, “from”: source or separation [PREP:ἀπό]; the tag gives the function of the phrase [CONV:D1].

461.n: TREE: Κῦρος depends on ἡγήσατο, not on δὲ as in the tree.

463.r: Agrees with the subject of the main clause [TREE]. Aorist stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as a single whole [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH]. Circumstantial participle with the main clause [SMYTH:2054].

467.r: Particular article: ἔθνη is a definite, identifiable referent [SMYTH:1119].

469.r: Article with the proper name Ἀσίᾳ [SMYTH:1136].

470.r: Dative with ἐν, “in, at”: place where [PREP:ἐν]; the tag gives the function of the phrase [CONV:D1].

472.r: αὐτόνομα is the predicate with ὄντα, said of ἔθνη: “finding the nations independent”. A predicate accusative is tagged AccDoubl [CONV:R5]; by agreement it could also take the object function of ἔθνη.

473.r: παραλαβὼν … τὰ ἔθνη αὐτόνομα ὄντα “finding the nations … independent”: the participle is predicative to the object, giving the state in which he found them [TR]. It is not after a verb of perceiving, so circumstantial comes first. Agrees with ἔθνη and takes its case function [TREE]. Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH].

474.r: ὁρμηθείς “setting out”: aorist passive in form, but ὁρμάομαι is a middle of motion [CONV:D3]. Agrees with the subject of the main clause [TREE]. Aorist stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as a single whole [SMYTH:1859]. Circumstantial participle with the main clause [SMYTH:2054].

476.r: Agrees with στρατιᾷ and takes its case function [TREE].

477.r: ὀλίγῃ Περσῶν στρατιᾷ “a small army of Persians”: the genitive of what the army consists of [SMYTH:1323].

478.r: Dative with σύν, “with”: accompaniment [PREP:σύν]; the tag gives the function of the phrase [CONV:D1].

479.r: Agrees with Μήδων and takes its case function [TREE].

481.r: ἡγήσατο “became leader of”: Holden, “imperium adeptus est, ‘became leader of’. For this use of the aorist (inceptive or ingressive) cf. ἦρξε, ἐπῆρξε” [COMM:en-holden-1887-books1-2-notes:18]. ἡγέομαι is middle-only; the project lists it with the mental middles (“consider”), though here it means “lead” [CONV:D3]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

484.r: Agrees with Ὑρκανίων and takes its case function [TREE].

488.r: Aorist indicative stating a single past event [SMYTH:1923]. καταστρέφομαι “subdue (to oneself)”: an indirect reflexive middle [SMYTH:1719]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

499.r: Agrees with Φρύγας and takes its case function [TREE].

509.r: ἦρξε “came to rule”: Holden names it with ἡγήσατο as the “inceptive or ingressive” aorist [COMM:en-holden-1887-books1-2-notes:18]. Active voice [MORPH]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

526.r: Agrees with ἐθνῶν and takes its case function [TREE].

528.r: Agrees with ἐθνῶν and takes its case function [TREE].

534.r: Particular article: ὀνόματα is a definite, identifiable referent [SMYTH:1119].

536.r: Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH]. Potential optative with ἄν [SMYTH:1824].

538.r: Aorist stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as a single whole [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH]. Dynamic infinitive completing ἔχοι [SMYTH:1989].

540.r: ἐπῆρξε “extended his rule over”: Holden–Shuckburgh, “ἐπῆρξε, inceptive aorist” [COMM:en-holden-shuckburgh-1902-book1:80]. Active voice [MORPH]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

544.r: Ἑλλήνων τῶν ἐν τῇ Ἀσίᾳ: the article repeated to attach the attributive phrase to the noun, “the Asiatic Greeks” [SMYTH:1158] [COMM:en-holden-shuckburgh-1902-book1:80].

546.r: Article with the proper name Ἀσίᾳ [SMYTH:1136].

547.r: Dative with ἐν, “in, at”: place where [PREP:ἐν]; the tag gives the function of the phrase [CONV:D1].

549.r: Agrees with the subject of ἐπῆρξε [TREE]. Aorist stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as a single whole [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH]. Circumstantial participle with ἐπῆρξε [SMYTH:2054].

552.r: Accusative with ἐπί, “to, against”: motion towards [PREP:ἐπί]; the tag gives the function of the phrase [CONV:D1].

554.n: TREE: Κυπρίων depends on ἐπῆρξε, not on καὶ as in the tree.
554.r: The genitive is governed by ἐπῆρξε, “he came to rule the Cyprians too” [SMYTH:1370]; καταβὰς ἐπὶ θάλατταν only gives the circumstance. Genitive governed by ἐπῆρξε [SMYTH:1341].

556.n: TREE: Αἰγυπτίων depends on ἐπῆρξε, not on καὶ as in the tree.
556.r: The genitive is governed by ἐπῆρξε, parallel to Κυπρίων [SMYTH:1370]. Genitive governed by ἐπῆρξε [SMYTH:1341].

560.r: Agrees with ἐθνῶν and takes its case function [TREE].

561.r: Particular article: ἐθνῶν is a definite, identifiable referent [SMYTH:1119].

563.r: ἦρξεν “he ruled over” sums up his reign as one fact; Miller: “He ruled over these nations” [TR]. The aorist can be felt as complexive [SMYTH:1927]; the plain tag is kept first [CONV:D2]. Active voice [MORPH]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

566.r: αὐτῷ ὁμογλώττων “of the same language as himself”: dative with a word of likeness [SMYTH:1500], tagged as a complement [CONV:R9]. Holden: “On the use of αὐτῷ as an indirect reflexive see HA. § 684a” [COMM:en-holden-1887-books1-2-notes:19].

567.r: Agrees with ἐθνῶν and takes its case function [TREE].

568.r: οὔτε … ὁμογλώττων ὄντων agrees with ἐθνῶν and is concessive; Holden: “though they did not speak the same language either with him or with each other” [COMM:en-holden-1887-books1-2-notes:19]. Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH].

571.r: ἀλλήλοις with ὁμογλώττων, “of the same language as one another”: dative with a word of likeness [SMYTH:1500] [CONV:R9].

575.r: Aorist indicative stating a single past event [SMYTH:1923]. δύναμαι “be able” is middle-only and fits none of the middle types well; the case is still open [CONV:D3] [CONV:R3]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

576.r: Aorist stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as a single whole [SMYTH:1859]. ἐφικνέομαι “reach” is middle-only, a middle of motion [CONV:D3]. Dynamic infinitive completing ἐδυνάσθη [SMYTH:1989].

579.r: Agrees with γῆν and takes its case function [TREE].

8031.r: δοκεῖ εἶναι “seems to be”: δοκέω with the infinitive [CONV:R7]. In indirect discourse the tense is that of the direct form [CONV:D7]. Active voice [MORPH].

8035.r: Present indicative of a present or general fact [MORPH]. Active voice [MORPH]. Indicative of a statement or question [MORPH].

8036.r: ὁρῶ σε τοιοῦτον ὄντα “I see you, being so handsome”: object of ὁρῶ [SMYTH:2110] [CONV:R4].

8038.r: Predicate in the accusative, agreeing with the accusative subject of ὄντα [SMYTH:1062]; the predicate accusative is tagged AccDoubl [CONV:R5].

8039.r: Miller: “because during that time I do not see you, who are so handsome” [TR]: the participle describes Cyrus rather than giving what is seen, so it is read as circumstantial; it can also be taken as supplementary after ὁράω [SMYTH:2110]. Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH].

8043.r: Article with the proper name Κῦρον [SMYTH:1136].

8044.r: Accusative subject of the main clause [SMYTH:1972].

8045.r: In indirect discourse the tense is that of the direct form [CONV:D7]. Active voice [MORPH]. γελάσαι continues the reported narrative, which depends on a verb of saying such as φασι or λέγεται: infinitive of indirect discourse [SMYTH:2017].

8048.r: τῶν ἔμπροσθεν δακρύων “his tears of a moment before”: the article makes the adverb ἔμπροσθεν attributive [SMYTH:1153].

8050.r: Holden: “ἐκ τῶν ἔμπροσθεν δακρύων, post priores lacrimas” [COMM:en-holden-1887-books1-2-notes:84]: ἐκ with the genitive, of the state out of which the laughter came, shading into time [PREP:ἐκ] [CONV:D1].

8052.r: In indirect discourse the tense is that of the direct form [CONV:D7]. Active voice [MORPH]. εἰπεῖν continues the reported narrative, which depends on a verb of saying such as φασι or λέγεται: infinitive of indirect discourse [SMYTH:2017].

8053.r: Dative governed by εἰπεῖν [SMYTH:1460]. Oblique αὐτός standing alone: the personal pronoun “him, her, it, them” [SMYTH:1212].

8054.r: εἰπεῖν αὐτῷ θαρρεῖν “told him to be of good cheer”: after a verb of saying used of a command the infinitive is not declarative [SMYTH:1997]. Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH].

8055.r: Holden: “θαρρεῖν ἀπιόντι, ‘to go back cheerfully’” [COMM:en-holden-1887-books1-2-notes:84]: the participle carries the main idea, a circumstantial participle agreeing with αὐτῷ [SMYTH:2062]. Present stem outside the indicative: aspect only, the action as ongoing [SMYTH:1859]. Active voice [MORPH].
